proposal.claim: Compensating for the oblique-incidence blue shift by designing a red-shifted normal-incidence center wavelength will improve visible reflectance at 45 degrees.
proposal.rationale: Compensating for the oblique-incidence blue shift by designing a red-shifted normal-incidence center wavelength will improve visible reflectance at 45 degrees.

predictions.controlled_conditions: Same 12-layer alternating stack, air incident, fused silica substrate, 45-degree unpolarized illumination.
predictions.reason: Thicker layers shift the stopband to longer wavelengths. If the baseline is still too blue-shifted at 45 degrees, further thickening should center the high-reflection band over the 450-650 nm range, increasing the integral mean.

predictions.controlled_conditions: Same 12-layer alternating stack, air incident, fused silica substrate, 45-degree unpolarized illumination.
predictions.reason: Shifting the reflection band toward longer wavelengths risks encroaching on the NIR transmission band (700+ nm), potentially reducing transmittance at the lower end of the NIR range.

limits: Absorptance from R/T closure is not independent energy validation.
No gradient calculation or extra forward probe performed.

proposal.claim: Breaking the quarter-wave symmetry by thickening the high-index layers relative to low-index layers can broaden the effective stopband at 45 degrees to cover the full visible spectrum.
proposal.rationale: Breaking the quarter-wave symmetry by thickening the high-index layers relative to low-index layers can broaden the effective stopband at 45 degrees to cover the full visible spectrum.

predictions.controlled_conditions: Same 12-layer order, substrate, medium, and angle.
predictions.reason: Increasing the optical thickness of the high-index layers relative to low-index layers may broaden the composite stopband or fill the polarization-induced dip, improving the integrated reflectance across the visible band.

limits: Absorptance from R/T closure is not independent energy validation.

proposal.claim: Increasing the total number of periods to the maximum allowed (24 layers) will maximize the depth of the visible reflection stopband, pushing mean reflectance closer to unity.
proposal.rationale: Increasing the total number of periods to the maximum allowed (24 layers) will maximize the depth of the visible reflection stopband, pushing mean reflectance closer to unity.

predictions.controlled_conditions: Same thickness parameters, doubled layer count.
predictions.reason: Doubling the number of periods from 6 to 12 (24 layers) significantly increases the number of interfering interfaces, which theoretically drives the reflectance in the stopband closer to 100%, thus increasing the mean reflectance.

limits: Absorptance from R/T closure is not independent energy validation.
